speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you have yellowish coloring of your skin and eyes, which indicates jaundice. Can you describe any other symptoms you've been experiencing, such as abdominal pain, fever, or dark urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your high-risk sexual history, do you have any nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite? I would also like to know if you've had any recent tattoos or new sexual partners. REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Tests

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST: 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT: 650 IU/L (elevated), TP Activity: < 40% (reduced), INR: 1.5 (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: These lab results indicate severe liver dysfunction, so I need to ask if you have experienced any confusion, disorientation, or sleep disturbances that might suggest hepatic encephalopathy? I also need to know if you have had any recent unprotected sex with new partners or used shared needles, as this would strongly point toward acute Hepatitis B or C. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis Serology Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the viral hepatitis panel is negative, I need to rule out other causes of acute liver failure. Have you taken any acetaminophen or consumed wild mushrooms recently? REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative viral and toxicology screens, I need to check for autoimmune causes or other metabolic issues. Have you experienced any joint pain, rash, or oral ulcers recently? REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune Liver Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: With viral, toxic, and autoimmune causes ruled out, I suspect a vascular issue like Budd-Chiari syndrome or Wilson's disease. Do you have any personal or family history of blood clots, or symptoms like tremors and Kayser-Fleischer rings? REQUEST TEST: Ceruloplasmin Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal ceruloplasmin and negative workup for common causes, I need to rule out ischemic hepatitis or other metabolic disorders. Have you experienced any recent episodes of severe hypotension, shock, or chest pain, and do you have any family history of liver disease or movement disorders? REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile

speaker: Doctor
text: The coagulation results confirm severe synthetic liver failure, but with standard causes ruled out, I need to investigate rare metabolic or infectious etiologies. Have you experienced any abdominal pain, right upper quadrant tenderness, or recent travel to areas endemic for Hepatitis E? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis E IgM

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the acute liver failure with coagulopathy and normal ceruloplasmin, I must rule out Wilson's disease despite the normal serum level, as it can be misleading in acute crisis. REQUEST TEST: 24-Hour Urine Copper

speaker: Doctor
text: With all major metabolic, viral, toxic, and autoimmune causes ruled out, and given the history of high-risk behavior and acute presentation, I suspect an atypical or seronegative infection or acute hepatitis A. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis A
